scenario: AITA for not jumping up and helping my parents bring in the groceries? I'm an adult and I pay rent if that helps. | I'm 33 years old and I've pretty much always lived with my parents. To me there's no shame in it because it's super cheap (they charge me $200, which honestly would be market rate where we live) and it has everything I want and need without the hassle of having to look for a new place to live. We get along most of the time but honestly I just avoid them. Recently the toilet flooded in my bathroom which means they are having to remodel my section of the house so we "run into" each other a lot more than when I used to lock myself in my room most of the time. Well today my parents went to Costco. When they got home I was sitting on the couch playing Apex and my mom asked me to get up and help them bring in groceries. I told her in a minute. I was honestly too into my game to notice that they made several trips back and forth and finally my dad told me to get my ass up. I told him I would in a minute. He said a minute is now and grabbed the controller out of my hand. It turned into a huge shouting match and now they are checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday (which is basically impossible). Of course they brought up my younger brother who is married with two kids and was just promoted at his job. They have their golden child of course but to throw his shit in my face is bullshit. I mean I guess I could have gotten up and helped them but to me because I pay rent that gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask me for stuff like helping with groceries or yard work. Am I the asshole in this situation?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm the asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what happened. I'm 33 years old and have been living with my parents most of my life. They charge me $200, which seems reasonable given where we live. I pay rent, so I feel like I should have some say in how I spend my time, right? Recently, there was a toilet flood in my bathroom, which means they had to remodel my section of the house. Because of this, we're running into each other a lot more than before. I used to lock myself in my room most of the time to avoid them, but now that's not possible. Today, my parents went to Costco. When they got home, I was sitting on the couch playing Apex Legends. My mom asked me to help bring in the groceries, and I told her I'd do it in a minute. Honestly, I was too into the game to notice that they made several trips back and forth. Finally, my dad told me to get my ass up, and I again said I'd do it in a minute. He got angry, grabbed the controller out of my hand, and it turned into a huge shouting match. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to have a place to live by Friday, which seems impossible. They also brought up my younger brother, who is married with two kids and just got promoted at his job. They're comparing me to him, which is really frustrating. I mean, I guess I could have gotten up and helped them, but to me, paying rent gives me the privilege to pretty much say no when they ask for help with groceries or yardwork. So, am I the asshole here? I need to think about this carefully. First, I should consider the dynamics of living with parents as an adult. It's not uncommon, but it does come with its own set of challenges. Paying rent is one thing, but living under the same roof means there are shared responsibilities and expectations. When my mom asked me to help with groceries, I told her I'd do it in a minute. That seems reasonable, but I was too engrossed in my game to notice that they were making multiple trips. That lack of awareness might have contributed to the conflict. When my dad told me to get up, and I again said I'd do it in a minute, that might have been the tipping point. Grabbing the controller and the shouting match that followed escalated the situation. Now, they're checking into a hotel and expecting me to find a place by Friday. That seems extreme, especially since finding a place to live in a short time frame is difficult. They also brought up my younger brother, which is a classic "golden child" scenario. Comparing siblings can be hurtful and unfair, especially when each person's circumstances are different. On the other hand, I feel like paying rent gives me some autonomy. I shouldn't have to drop everything every time they ask for help. But living with others means there are shared responsibilities. I also need to consider the emotional impact of the shouting match. It's not healthy for anyone to yell like that, and it probably made things worse. So, am I the asshole? I think there's some responsibility on both sides. I should have been more considerate of their needs, especially since we're living in the same space. Ignoring their requests and being too absorbed in my game contributed to the conflict. On the flip side, expecting me to find a place by Friday is unrealistic and adds unnecessary stress. They should have communicated their concerns more calmly and rationally instead of resorting to yelling. In the end, both parties could have handled the situation better. I should have been more responsive to their requests, and they should have addressed the issue without escalating it into a shouting match. So, I think I'm partially the asshole for not being more considerate and responsive, but the situation could have been handled better by both sides.
